statement.p: Find \mathbf{r}(t) and \mathbf{v}(t) given acceleration \mathbf{a}(t)=\left\lt t,9\right>, initial velocity \mathbf{v}(0)=\left\lt -2,3\right>, and initial position \mathbf{r}(0)=\left\lt 0,0\right>.
Usage: To enter a vector, for example \langle x,y,z\rangle, type \lt x, y, z \gt

static.solution: \mathbf{a}(t) to obtain the velocity vector: \mathbf{v}(t) = \int_0^t \left\lt u,9\right> du = \left.\left\langle \frac{u^2}{2},9 u\right\rangle\right|_0^t+\mathbf{v}_0 = \left\langle \frac{t^2}{2},9 t\right\rangle+\mathbf{v}_0. The initial condition \mathbf{v}(0)=\left\lt -2,3\right> gives: \mathbf{v}(0) = \langle 0,0\rangle+\mathbf{v}_0=\left\lt -2,3\right> so \mathbf{v}_0=\left\lt -2,3\right> and we obtain \mathbf{v}(t) = \left\langle \frac{t^2}{2},9 t\right\rangle+\left\lt -2,3\right> = \left\langle \frac{t^2}{2} - 2,9 t+3\right\rangle. We now integrate the velocity vector to find \mathbf{r}(t): \begin{array}{rcl} \mathbf{r}(t) \amp =\amp \displaystyle\int_0^t \left\langle \frac{u^2}{2} - 2,9 u+3\right\rangle\ du \\ \amp =\amp \left.\left\langle \frac{u^3}{6} - 2 u,\frac{9 u^2}{2}+3 u\right\rangle\right|_0^t +\mathbf{r}_0 \\ \amp =\amp \left\langle \frac{t^3}{6} - 2 t,\frac{9 t^2}{2}+3 t\right\rangle+\mathbf{r}_0 \end{array} The initial condition \mathbf{r}(0)=\langle 0,0\rangle gives \mathbf{r}_0=\langle 0,0\rangle, so \mathbf{r}(t)=\left\langle \frac{t^3}{6} - 2 t,\frac{9 t^2}{2}+3 t\right\rangle.
